items.title: Good Companionship Opens: Eight Marks of a True Spiritual Friend

items.zh: 云何名善友性？謂八因緣故，應知一切種圓滿善友性。何等為八？謂如有一，安住禁戒、具足多聞、能有所證、性多哀愍、心無厭倦、善能堪忍、無有怖畏、語具圓滿。
items.en: Within the Basic Section, in the Ground of the Hearer-Disciples, the first yogic process, the Ground of Setting Out Towards Liberation, the fourth part of the third chapter … What is meant by the nature of a good friend? By eight causal factors, one should understand a good friend's nature as complete in every respect. What are the eight? It is like one who abides in restraint, is possessed of extensive learning, has genuine attainment, is deeply compassionate by nature, is tireless in mind, is well able to endure, is free of fear, and is complete in speech.

items.title: The First Mark: Abiding in Restraint

items.zh: 云何名為安住禁戒？謂安住具戒，善能守護別解律儀，如前廣說樂沙門性、樂婆羅門性、為自調伏、為自寂靜、為自涅槃，修行正行。如是名為安住禁戒。
items.en: What is meant by abiding in restraint? It means abiding fully in discipline, skilfully guarding the vows of individual liberation, as explained at length before — delighting in the nature of a true renunciant, delighting in the nature of one who has driven out unwholesome states, practising correctly for the sake of taming oneself, for the sake of one's own peace, and for the sake of one's own nirvana. This is called abiding in restraint.

items.title: Section: The Second Mark — Extensive Learning and Its Nine Qualities

items.zh: 云何名為具足多聞？謂若有法宣說開示，初中後善，文義巧妙，獨一、圓滿、清白、梵行。於如是類眾多妙法，能善受持，言善通利、意善尋思、見善通達。如是名為具足多聞。
items.en: What is meant by extensive learning? It means that, regarding a teaching proclaimed and explained — good in the beginning, good in the middle, and good in the end, its meaning subtle and its wording skilful, unique, complete, pure, and holy — one is able to receive and retain many such excellent teachings well: fluent in their language, skilfully investigating their meaning, and thoroughly penetrating [the teachings] through direct seeing. This is called extensive learning.

items.title: Section: The Third Mark — Genuine Attainment's Twenty Perceptions

items.zh: 云何名為能有所證？謂能證得勝無常想、無常苦想、苦無我想、厭逆食想、一切世間不可樂想、有過患想、斷想、離想、滅想、死想、不淨想、青瘀想、膿爛想、破壞想、膖脹想、噉食想、血塗想、離散想、骨鎖想、觀察空想。
items.en: What is meant by genuine attainment? It means being able to realise: the perception of surpassing impermanence, the perception of impermanence as suffering, the perception of suffering as non-self, the perception of revulsion towards food, the perception of the entire world as unlovable, the perception of its inherent flaws, the perception of cutting-off, the perception of detachment, the perception of cessation, the perception of death, the perception of impurity, and the perceptions of a corpse turning livid, festering, decaying, bloating, being devoured, smeared with blood, scattered apart, and reduced to bare bone — and, finally, the perception of examined emptiness.

items.title: Absorptions, Immeasurables, Fruits, Powers — Genuine Attainment Continues

items.zh: 復能證得最初靜慮、第二靜慮、第三靜慮、第四靜慮、空無邊處、識無邊處、無所有處、最後非想非非想處。又能證得慈悲喜捨，或預流果、或一來果、或不還果、或神境通、或宿住通、或天耳通、或死生通、或心差別通、或阿羅漢。具八解脫靜慮等定，有大堪能，具大勢力，能善為他現三神變教授教誡。
items.en: Furthermore, one can realise the first, second, third, and fourth absorptions, the sphere of infinite space, the sphere of infinite consciousness, the sphere of nothingness, and finally the sphere of neither perception nor non-perception. One can also realise loving-kindness, compassion, sympathetic joy, and equanimity; or the fruit of stream-entry, of once-returning, or of non-returning; or the supernormal power of miraculous ability, of recollecting past lives, of the divine ear, of seeing beings' death and rebirth, or of knowing others' minds; or arhatship itself. Possessing the eight liberations and such meditative attainments, one has great capability and great strength, and is able to skilfully instruct and guide others by manifesting three kinds of miraculous display.

items.zh: 三神變者，一、神力神變，二、記說神變，三、教導神變。如是名為能有所證。

items.title: Section: The Fourth Mark — Deep Compassion, Mapped to the Four Immeasurables

items.zh: 云何名為為性哀愍？謂於他所常起悲憐，樂與其義、樂與其利、樂與其樂、樂與猗觸、樂與安隱。如是名為為性哀愍。
items.en: What is meant by deep compassion by nature? It means constantly feeling compassion for others — delighting in giving them benefit, delighting in giving them advantage, delighting in giving them ease, delighting in giving them the contact of [meditative] pliancy, and delighting in giving them peace. This is called deep compassion by nature.

items.title: The Fifth Mark: A Tireless Mind for Teaching

items.zh: 云何名為心無厭倦？謂善能示現、善能教導、善能讚勵、善能慶慰，處於四眾宣說正法，不辭勞倦，翹勤無墮，起發圓滿，為性好樂，發勤精進。如是名為心無厭倦。
items.en: What is meant by a tireless mind? It means being skilled at demonstrating, skilled at instructing, skilled at encouraging, and skilled at rejoicing with others — teaching the true Dharma before the fourfold assembly without begrudging the effort, diligent and never lazy, arousing complete energy, delighting in it by nature, and generating sustained diligence. This is called a tireless mind.

items.title: Section: The Sixth Mark — Forbearance, Towards Both Hostility and Hardship

items.zh: 云何名為善能堪忍？謂罵不報罵、瞋不報瞋、打不報打、弄不報弄、堪耐椎杵。於諸逼迫、縛錄、禁閉、捶打、毀辱、迫愶、斫截眾苦事中，自推己過，以業異熟為所依趣，終不於他發生憤恚，亦不懷恨隨眠不捨。如是雖遭輕陵毀辱，而其本性都無變改，唯常於彼思為義利。又能堪忍寒熱、飢渴、蚊虻、風日、蛇蠍惡觸，他所干犯、磣毒語言，身內所生猛利、堅勁、辛楚、切心、奪命苦受，為性堪忍，能有容納。如是名為善能堪忍。
items.en: What is meant by genuine forbearance? It means not repaying abuse with abuse, not repaying anger with anger, not repaying a blow with a blow, not repaying mockery with mockery, enduring even a beating. … Attributing the fault to oneself, taking it as the ripening of one's own past actions, one never gives rise to resentment towards another, nor harbours a lasting grudge. … One is also able to endure cold and heat, hunger and thirst, mosquitoes and gnats, wind and sun, the bite of snakes and scorpions, others' unjust intrusions, cruel and poisonous speech, and even severe, sharp, agonising, life-threatening pain arising within the body itself — enduring all of it by nature, with genuine capacity to bear it. This is called genuine forbearance.

items.title: The Seventh Mark: Fearlessness Before an Audience

items.zh: 云何名為無有怖畏？謂處大眾說正法時，心無怯劣、聲無戰掉、辯無誤失，終不由彼怯懼因緣，為諸怖畏之所逼切，腋不流汗、身毛不
items.en: What is meant by fearlessness? It means that, when teaching the true Dharma before a large assembly, the mind is not timid or weak, the voice does not tremble, and one's reasoning is without error — never oppressed by fear born of timidity, the armpits do not sweat, and the body's hair does not stand on end.

items.title: Section: The Eighth Mark — Complete Speech, and All Eight Marks Close

items.zh: 云何名為語具圓滿？謂彼成就最上首語、極美妙語、甚顯了語、易悟解語、樂欲聞語、無違逆語、無所依語、無邊際語。如是名為語具圓滿，言詞巧妙。
items.en: What is meant by complete speech? It means being accomplished in speech that leads towards nirvana above all else, speech of the utmost beauty, speech that is thoroughly clear, speech that is easily understood, speech people delight in hearing, speech free of anything objectionable, speech free of any hidden agenda, and speech of boundless scope. This is called complete speech, skilful in every word.

items.title: Section: Five Things a Qualified Spiritual Friend Can Do — Beginning With Skilful Admonishment

items.zh: 成就如是八種因緣，善能諫舉、善作憶念、善能教授、善能教誡、善說正法。云何名為善能諫舉？謂若有餘，於增上戒毀犯尸羅，於增上軌毀犯軌則，由見聞疑能正諫舉，真實不以虛妄，應時不以非時，饒益不以衰損，柔軟不以麁獷，善友不以憎嫉。如是名為善能諫舉。
items.en: Having accomplished these eight causal factors, one is skilled at admonishing, skilled at reminding, skilled at instructing, skilled at guiding, and skilled at teaching the true Dharma. What is meant by skilful admonishment? It means that, when another has violated the precepts or broken the code of conduct, having seen it, heard of it, or come to suspect it, one admonishes them correctly: truthfully, not falsely; at the proper time, not an improper time; for their genuine benefit, not their harm; gently, not harshly; as a true friend, not out of resentment or envy. This is called skilful admonishment.

blocks.text: Fascicle 25 completes the fourteen provisions: good friendship, hearing and reflecting, freedom from obstacles, generosity, and the "ornaments" of a renunciant. It is fully translated. Today: the eight marks of a true spiritual friend.
Master Cháng Bǎi quotes the Buddha to Ānanda: "the spiritual friend is the whole of the holy life." The treatise lists eight marks of such a friend.

**Abiding in restraint**: full moral discipline. Venerable Miào Jìng: delighting in the renunciant's nature is the virtue of wisdom; in the brahmin's, purity. **Extensive learning**: a teaching "good in the beginning, middle, and end", heard, recited, investigated, and penetrated. Venerable Miào Jìng: fluency is hearing; investigation is reflection; penetration is cultivation.

The friend has realised perceptions such as impermanence, suffering, non-self, the impurities, as well as the absorptions, immeasurables, and fruits. Venerable Miào Jìng: the impurity perceptions cannot cut afflictions, "but they are powerful: able to hold afflictions down".

**Compassion**: delighting in giving others benefit and ease. **Tirelessness**: "skilled at demonstrating, instructing, encouraging, rejoicing", teaching without begrudging effort. **Forbearance**: "not repaying abuse with abuse… attributing the fault to oneself, taking it as the ripening of one's own past actions". Master Cháng Bǎi: the spiritual friend thinks differently from ordinary people.

Before a large assembly, "the mind is not timid, the voice does not tremble". Speech leads towards nirvāṇa, is clear and pleasing. Master Cháng Bǎi: but don't say too much: "if only one chicken is left, can it eat all that feed?"

subs.head: Five things a good friend does

blocks.text: Admonishes, reminds, instructs, guides, teaches. Venerable Miào Jìng on admonishing: a good friend would not correct you before the assembly and make you lose face.

quiz.q: Citing the Āgamas, how does Master Cháng Bǎi say the Buddha corrected Ānanda about spiritual friends?
options: the spiritual friend is the whole of the holy life, not half
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: "Ānanda, the spiritual friend is the whole of the holy life; with a spiritual friend one can be expected to cultivate the noble path diligently." Ānanda had said it was half.

quiz.q: How does Venerable Miào Jìng distinguish "delighting in the renunciant's nature" from "delighting in the brahmin's nature"?
options: the first is the virtue of wisdom, the second the virtue of cutting off
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: delighting in the renunciant's nature is, in brief, the realm of wisdom — the virtue of wisdom; delighting in the brahmin's nature is the virtue of cutting off. The English "one who has driven out unwholesome states" matches the latter.

quiz.q: What qualities does the teaching held in extensive learning have, and how does Master Cháng Bǎi explain "good in the beginning" and "in the middle"?
options: good in beginning, middle, and end, subtle and skilful, unique, complete, pure, holy; the first gives joy on hearing, the middle brings no difficulty in practice
quiz.why: "Good in the beginning, good in the middle, and good in the end, its meaning subtle and its wording skilful, unique, complete, pure, and holy." Master Cháng Bǎi: good in the beginning means it brings joy when first heard; good in the middle means practising as taught involves no difficulty.

quiz.q: Can the nine perceptions cut off afflictions, according to Venerable Miào Jìng?
options: they cannot cut them off, but are powerful enough to suppress them
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: the nine perceptions cannot cut off afflictions, but they are powerful — able to hold afflictions down so they do not stir.

quiz.q: In deep compassion, what five things does one delight in giving, and how does Venerable Miào Jìng read "nature"?
options: money, house, car, clothes, food; innate temperament
fame, profit, power, rank, influence; gender
benefit, advantage, ease, joyful contact, peace; "nature" is mind — the mind itself is compassionate
quiz.why: "Constantly feeling compassion for others — delighting in giving them benefit, delighting in giving them advantage, delighting in giving them ease, delighting in giving them joyful contact, and delighting in giving them peace." Venerable Miào Jìng: "nature" here means mind — the mind is compassionate, deeply sympathetic.

quiz.q: How does one who has genuine forbearance regard harm from others?
options: attributing the fault to oneself as the ripening of past actions, never resentful, holding no grudge
quiz.why: "Attributing the fault to oneself, taking it as the ripening of one's own past actions, one never gives rise to resentment towards another, nor harbours a lasting grudge." Venerable Miào Jìng: it is because of wrongs I did in past lives that I now receive this result.

quiz.q: To what does Master Cháng Bǎi attribute fearlessness when teaching a large assembly?
options: holding pure precepts and having extensive learning
quiz.why: The mind is not timid, the voice does not tremble, the armpits do not sweat, the hair does not stand on end. Master Cháng Bǎi: because such a friend holds pure precepts and is extensively learned, they teach fearlessly before large assemblies.
